analysis:
The change to docs/reference/configuration.md is documentation only: it bumps the "Last updated" date (line 3) and adds one row at head line 313 for `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL`. The row is visible only in the patch excerpt, not in the numbered head text. It describes an exact-`0`-disable switch, default on. It governs whether full-attention prompt chunks use one fused `.causal` SDPA call or 128-query blocks. It is read once per process and is not forwarded to LaunchAgents. No code, authorization, attestation, key handling, wire protocol or cache storage behavior is changed in the supplied evidence.

Relevant threats examined: T-041 and TB-007 (prefix cache and the TTFT timing oracle). The new variable is a performance-path switch. It does not change cache enablement, TTL, encryption, HMAC lookup naming, salt scoping or account isolation. It could shift TTFT timing characteristics, which the accepted SEC-035 oracle already covers, but nothing indicates any change to cache hit/miss behavior. The documented behavior also does not widen the LaunchAgent environment allow-list, so installed daemons are unaffected.

Remaining questions are outside the supplied evidence. The actual implementation in `libs/mlx-swift-lm/.../AttentionV1.swift` was not supplied, so correctness and numerical equivalence of the fused causal path are not verified. Any sensitivity of timing or memory behavior to this path was also not reviewed. A code change is likely part of the same PR in other units not supplied here. The numbered base text units were limited to the documentation lines supplied. No security regression is established from these docs.
